subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept `@openclaw/mxc-sandbox` as an official external plugin with `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, packaged native MXC executor binaries, `node-pty` install scripts, and upstream base64-argv config transport?
rationale: This is an intentional first-party sandbox/security boundary and dependency graph expansion; code review can verify the implementation shape, but only maintainers/security can accept the native dependency and exposure model.

options.title: Approve Exact Boundary
options.body: Admin/secops review and approve the current head dependency graph and accept the preview MXC SDK argv transport for this opt-in plugin.

options.title: Pause For Safer Transport
options.body: Hold the PR until upstream MXC provides a non-argv config transport or the plugin can avoid exposing sandbox config through process arguments.

options.title: Keep Outside Official Core
options.body: Decline first-party adoption for now and leave MXC experimentation to a community/ClawHub plugin until the dependency and sandbox boundary mature.

recommendation.title: Approve Exact Boundary
recommendation.body: Admin/secops review and approve the current head dependency graph and accept the preview MXC SDK argv transport for this opt-in plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to steipete and his current-main history covers the closest sandbox/plugin ownership boundary.
